items.title: First residents move into Affiniti, about 3,000 rental homes behind the Promenades
items.summary: Cogir's Affiniti project began move-ins on July 1 in its first 14-storey building, Mostra+. It plans about 3,000 rental units in 17 buildings, and about 4,700 units with the neighbouring Quartier des Promenades.
items.takeaway: The largest new-patient opportunity in the St-Bruno area, with new arrivals for several years. Target the Promenades sector with new-patient offers and online booking, and greet each new building as it opens.

items.title: Sabourin sector plan: 600 apartments and 259 townhouses in phase 1
items.summary: The city's update for montée Sabourin lists 600 multi-family units and 259 townhouses in the first residential phase. Council approval of the master plan is expected in winter 2026–2027.
items.takeaway: Not built yet, so this is a later wave. Townhouses usually mean families, so plan children's and family messaging for when it opens.

items.title: Liveo's first 12-storey tower opens on boulevard René-Lévesque
items.summary: The first tower, with about 284 rental units, welcomed residents in July. The project at 1000 boulevard René-Lévesque was approved for about 600 units in two phases, and the second phase has no published date.
items.takeaway: Hundreds of new rental households who may not have a local dentist yet. New-patient offers, mobile search ads and easy online booking suit this kind of building.

items.title: Square Châteauguay phase 2 adds 104 rental units
items.summary: Two buildings at boulevard Rousseau and rue Principale, a project of about $25 million, with completion planned for June to July 2026.
items.takeaway: Another cluster of new renters near the centre of Châteauguay. Combine it with Liveo in one new-resident campaign.

items.title: 55 townhouses on chemin du Christ-Roi
items.summary: A townhouse project by the builder, with delivery planned for April 2026.
items.takeaway: Townhouses tend to bring families. A good fit for children's first visits and family booking.

items.title: Proposed 12-storey building with 256 homes at 20 boulevard Maple
items.summary: The city held a public meeting on a resolution to allow the building. Its current status isn't published.
items.takeaway: One to watch rather than act on. The city's list of real-estate projects is the place to follow it.

items.title: The Montérégie keeps growing while Quebec stalls
items.source: Institut de la statistique du Québec
items.summary: The ISQ's 2026 update keeps Quebec's population roughly stable, but projects the Montérégie to grow by 3% to 5.6% by 2051. The government's regional portrait projects about 2% growth for the Montérégie from 2025 to 2030, against a small decline for Quebec.
items.takeaway: South Shore suburbs remain among the few growing markets in Quebec, so new-patient spending there is less of a gamble than elsewhere in the province.

items.title: Quebec dentists can now offer Botox, with training
items.summary: The Ordre des dentistes du Québec (ODQ) allows trained dentists to inject botulinum toxin for cosmetic and therapeutic uses. Training providers describe a path in levels, with uses such as bruxism and jaw pain, and with dermal fillers only at the highest level.
items.takeaway: Suits areas where older professionals are the main patient group, and therapeutic uses fit existing patients with bruxism. Advertise only what your training level allows, don't call a course "ODQ-certified", and check the ODQ's advertising rules first.

items.title: The Canadian Dental Care Plan now reaches more than 6.5 million people
items.summary: The federal plan covers uninsured residents with family income under $90,000. It pays after other public plans such as the RAMQ, and not every Quebec clinic takes part.
items.takeaway: Patients search for clinics that accept the plan. If you do, say so plainly, especially to retirees and lower-income families. Cosmetic work is outside the plan, so it stays private-pay.

items.title: Cosmetic demand: whitening leads, bonding is growing
items.summary: Practice and industry blogs rank whitening as the most requested cosmetic treatment, followed by composite bonding, veneers and clear aligners. These are marketing sources, not official data, and their market sizes disagree.
items.takeaway: Use whitening as the entry offer and follow up with bonding or aligners. These are private-pay services, so promote them where household incomes are higher.

items.title: What the RAMQ covers for children under 10
items.source: Protégez-vous, with the Protecteur du citoyen
items.summary: Exams, X-rays and anesthesia are free for insured children under 10. Cleanings, scaling and fluoride are not covered.
items.takeaway: In young-family areas, lead with free exams for children under 10, and be clear up front about what parents pay for.
